**The master manuscript now obtains a charged, smoothly marked disk throughout the full subcritical range \(I^+(M)<2T\), where \(T=4\pi^2\).** On any hypothetical nonstandard smooth homotopy four-sphere in this range, every minimizing sequence has a subsequence with definite Weyl energy of one fixed chirality on both sides of the disk boundary. Its two-sided collar can carry arbitrarily little original curvature relative to the core charge. The remaining descent step is to repair this actual collar at a cost smaller than the energy saved, while preserving positive Yamabe sign. A second result strengthens smooth recognition. Write \(e\) for either total chiral Weyl energy and \(L\) for the larger of the two top Weyl eigenvalues. For some universal \(\eta>0\),
\[
\inf_{Y([g])>0}\left(4e+3\int_M L^2\,dV\right)\le 8T+\eta
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad M\cong_{\mathrm{diff}}S^4.
\]
The infimum can be unattained. The proof gives no numerical value for \(\eta\). In the remaining case where the spectral deficit tends to zero, both chiral energies are captured to arbitrary tolerance, and trace-free Ricci energy must concentrate on sets of vanishing volume in the modified Yamabe metric. An explicit fiber rescaling makes eta zero. The interior energy and Yamabe sign of a filling with that rescaled boundary remain open. No additional smooth type was recognized.

All six source and PDF generations match the previous assessment. We can now enlarge the original charged disk, preserving its inner marking, so that the raw exterior carries less than \(T\) in both chiralities throughout \(I^+(M)<2T\). The larger boundary can leave the original comparison ball. I’m checking its repair allowance alongside a separate result about where modified Ricci curvature can concentrate.

The large-disk calculation now gives a quantitative obstruction. After finitely many enlargements, straightening only a collar of vanishing incoming curvature must reach the \(2T\) wall on any surviving nonstandard type. A subcritical repair would have to lower energy inside the disk. The original small disk remains a separate candidate. On the eta-zero Mazur face, independent calculations also found zero spin APS index, so that boundary test leaves the filling question open.

The closed-case check gives a stronger conclusion. In each fixed band \(e\le 2T-\delta\), only finitely many nonstandard smooth types can carry a positive Bach-flat class. If any do, their least spectral deficit is attained and positive. This rules out an exact closed Bach-flat explanation for a sequence whose deficit tends to zero. It still leaves arbitrary minimizing sequences without the compactness needed to extract such a limit.

The public Lean import confirms the disk-saving inequality with the positive cap, its smooth identification and its energy comparison as explicit hypotheses. I’m checking the four rebuilt PDFs against independent builds and recording which geometric steps remain open.

**The charged-disk calculation now gives a lower bound on what a repair must accomplish.** Starting from the actual marked disk, one enlargement leaves less than \(T=4\pi^2\) of physical Weyl energy in each chirality on the exterior throughout \(I^+(M)<2T\). The enlargement preserves the original disk and its marking. After a fixed number of enlargements, any matched repair that stays below \(2T\) and gives a positive cap on the original smooth type must remove more than the uniform gap \(\varepsilon_*\) from the disk side in **each** chirality. Straightening a collar with vanishing incoming curvature cannot supply that saving. A strict repair on the original smaller disk remains open.

**The closed alternative is narrower.** For every fixed \(\delta>0\), only finitely many nonstandard oriented smooth homotopy-sphere types can carry a positive Bach-flat class with \(e\le 2T-\delta\). If any do, their least spectral deficit is attained and strictly positive. This excludes exact Bach-flat classes along a sequence in that band whose deficit tends to zero. For arbitrary minimizing sequences, a smooth filled base satisfying the whole-base marking hypotheses must be conformally round. A restart through its single charged exit can still occur.

On the eta-zero Mazur face, the spin Dirac operator is invertible and the ordinary spin APS index vanishes. The qualifying positive filling remains open. At separated physical quantiles, an integral bound on the radial Jacobian now suffices to select a low-curvature window. Establishing that bound and the proper smooth embeddings on the actual sequence remains open. **No additional smooth type was recognized.**
